doc.title: vZDC–USN Virtual LOA
doc.summary: Coordination between vZDC and United States Navy Virtual / VSOA partners: special use airspace scheduling, activation and clearance, formation flights, carrier (CATCC) operations, intercepts and aerial refueling.

items.title: Purpose, scope and disclaimer
items.text: Establishes procedures between Virtual Washington ARTCC (vZDC) and United States Navy Virtual (USNv) for USNv operations in the ZDC AOR: SUA scheduling/activation, SUA entry phraseology, return-to-base coordination, release of airspace to non-NAS facilities, and ATC service by USNv personnel. Applies to USNv and all Virtual Special Operations Association (VSOA) partners per VATSIM-POL-Special Operations 8.2 and 8.4. Simulation only; no FAA/DoD affiliation.

items.title: ZDC controls SUA; releases to VSOA on request
items.text: vZDC retains sole jurisdiction over ZDC controlled airspace. SUA (ATCAA, MOA, Restricted, Warning areas) is controlled by ZDC and may be delegated to authorized VSOA pilots and facilities. vZDC will release SUA to VSOA pilots and other authorized operations upon request when in accordance with this agreement.

items.title: Pilots and controllers follow VATSIM/vZDC policy
items.text: VSOA pilots comply with all standard VATSIM ATC procedures including the VATSIM Special Operations Policy. All controllers, regardless of organization, comply with this LOA and applicable vZDC policy.

items.title: USNv visiting controllers (S3, S2)
items.text: USNv controllers with an S3 rating are accepted on the vZDC visiting roster with full privileges, including staffing any non-Tier 1 facility; they must serve all users regardless of affiliation. S2 USNv controllers are accepted when authorized under VATUSA's S2 Visiting Controller exception policy.

items.title: Stay in SUA; IFR separation from SUA boundary
items.text: VSOA pilots remain within cleared SUA until cleared out by the controlling agency. vZDC provides standard IFR separation from the SUA boundary for all non-participating aircraft. VSOA pilots will not cancel IFR when done with working airspace if returning directly to base.

items.title: Traffic alerts; keep non-participants clear of SUA
items.text: vZDC provides traffic alerts to the lead aircraft when non-participating aircraft not under vZDC control enter active SUA, broadcast on the assigned working frequency. Non-participating IFR aircraft are issued routing or vectors to always remain clear of all SUA.

items.title: Mission working frequency managed in vNAS
items.text: vZDC provides a designated mission working frequency for aircraft to monitor while in activated SUA, managed by ZDC/FE within vNAS Data Admin.

items.title: Deconfliction, facilities support, scheduling module
items.text: VSOA partners deconflict missions in the same SUA; vZDC clears aircraft into SUA as scheduled or as real-time requests permit and does not manage shared airspace agreements. vZDC provides vNAS and AFV facility support as directed by ZDC/ATM, and an SUA scheduling module on vzdc.org requiring the pilot's VATSIM credential.

items.title: VSOA flight plans: file IFR; 'VFR FP' remark
items.text: VSOA pilots complete an IFR flight plan for all operations (equivalent to DD-175/DD-1801). Pilots planning VFR put "VFR FP" in remarks and the controller amends the flight plan to VFR; routing and nonstandard requests go in remarks. For scheduled SUA include the mission number in remarks; for unscheduled SUA include the SUA complex (e.g. W72A). Any vzdc.org reservation, even under 24 hours, counts as scheduled. Pilots remain on assigned squawk unless instructed; IFR is preferred.
items.restr: Amend to VFR if remarks 'VFR FP'

items.title: SUA scheduling: 24-hour rule
items.text: SUA scheduling is through www.vzdc.org by any member authorized by their VSOA. Airspace scheduled at least 24 hours in advance will be accommodated by all vZDC controllers; less than 24 hours (including real-time requests) is accommodated workload permitting.

items.title: SUA activation and adjacent warning areas
items.text: Activation is by the controller responsible for the airspace containing the SUA. Scheduled SUA is accommodated with other traffic; unscheduled at controller's discretion. Pilots filed to SUA are assumed to proceed from departure to the SUA with no intermediate stop. ZDC coordinates with ZJX and ZNY for warning areas in their AORs and states in the clearance if adjacent-facility airspace is not released; otherwise the entire airspace is granted as cleared.

items.title: SUA departure release (different controllers)
items.text: When the controller providing ATCT duties is not the one managing the SUA, the ATCT controller notifies the controller of the airspace containing the SUA (or overlying ZDC sector if unknown) that an aircraft has an SUA clearance and its expected departure time, then notifies again when the aircraft has a departure release.

items.title: SUA activation time
items.text: Controllers show airspace active no later than receipt of the departure release notification, but do not begin activation until initial communications with the aircraft taking the airspace has occurred (scheduling alone does not activate it).

items.title: SUA clearance; release to MRU/ARU/AWACS
items.text: The controller responsible for the airspace containing the SUA issues the clearance regardless of who monitors it. If an MRU, ARU or AWACS will be used, the controller releases the SUA to that agency on request, but aircraft must still receive an airspace clearance before reaching the SUA and an instruction to change to working frequency.

items.title: SUA clearance phraseology
items.text: [CALLSIGN] CLEARED INTO [SUA NAME], [BOTTOM ALTITUDE] THROUGH [TOP ALTITUDE], WORKING FREQUENCY [FREQUENCY], REPORT FIVE MINUTES PRIOR TO R-T-B ON [FREQUENCY], FREQUENCY CHANGE APPROVED. Examples: BACON ONE ONE into W72A FL200 through FL600 on 129.65; TOAST FIVE ONE into W386 surface through FL300 on 129.65 with "USE CAUTION JELLY TWO TWO IN AIRSPACE".

items.title: Transfer of control to MRU/ARU/AWACS
items.text: vZDC completes an automated handoff to the MRU/ARU/AWACS the SUA has been released to when automation supports it; otherwise transfer of control is coordinated manually in the vZDC TeamSpeak server.

items.title: SUA exit and return to base
items.text: Five minutes prior to R-T-B, pilots notify ATC on the assigned frequency and advise of any split-ups or uncoordinated requests. When ready for R-T-B, they advise ATC and ATC issues further clearance.

items.title: VSOA controllers staffing ZDC facilities
items.text: VSOA controllers on the vZDC Visiting Controller Roster may control any unrestricted ZDC facility, using CRC and complying with all vZDC and facility procedures.

items.title: Formation flights: remarks and squawks
items.text: Indicate total aircraft in the formation in remarks (e.g. 3/F18). Standard formation assumed unless lead advises otherwise: lead squawks the assigned code, others squawk standby. Non-standard formation (including radar in trail): lead squawks the assigned code, trail aircraft squawk the non-discrete subset (e.g. lead 2355, trail 2300), intermediate aircraft squawk standby.

items.title: Carrier ops with CATCC: 100NM / SFC-10,000 release
items.text: Ships operate no closer than 100nm from the shoreline except operations fully within activated warning airspace. CATCC provides a K-fix (e.g. KW39A) or named waypoint as the ship location; ZDC releases surface to 10,000 MSL within 100NM of that reference fix to CATCC, coordinating with ZNY and ZJX when scheduled through vZDC. Reference fix updates are passed as the ship moves.

items.title: CATCC transfer: ZDC assigns 11000 inbound, CATCC 10000 out
items.text: Transfer of control is via automated handoff when available, otherwise manual coordination. ZDC assigns 11000ft to aircraft inbound to CATCC control; CATCC assigns 10000ft to departing aircraft. CATCC coordinates aircraft using SUA per paragraph 5c1.

items.title: CATCC in warning areas; ops when ZDC closed
items.text: If all operations stay within warning airspace, ZDC may release the warning area(s) to CATCC and use released boundaries and coordinated altitudes as the CATCC boundary for handoffs. When ZDC is closed, CATCC may operate within warning airspace surface to 10,000ft after a scheduling notice on the vZDC website; if ZDC opens, CATCC contacts ZDC to coordinate.

items.title: Carrier ops without CATCC
items.text: Airspace is scheduled and activated per this letter, from the surface to the highest altitude requested, as a continuous volume. Other SUA clearance and activation procedures apply.

items.title: Aircraft interception procedures
items.text: Pilots advertise availability for intercept by private message (one message only). Controllers request intercepts by private message with aircraft type, callsign, cause and approximate position; if available, the controller issues an abbreviated IFR clearance and taxi. Airborne, controllers guide with route/vector clearances and assign altitudes for vertical separation. Interceptors use guard and standard intercept procedures, not the ATC frequency unless instructed. Controllers may suspend intercepts at any time; the interceptor tells ZDC whether it will follow to destination or break off.

items.title: Aerial refueling: 3000ft block, MARSA
items.text: Expect a 3000ft block for aerial refueling. ZDC assigns altitudes ensuring at least 1000ft vertical separation before join-up and may verify MARSA before assigning the block. After AR, pilots separate by 1000ft within the block, advise complete and state intentions. AR tracks must be filed by named waypoint or fix/radial/distance (e.g. ORF270015); larger blocks may be approved. Random refueling may be approved along any filed route segment.

items.title: Authority, revisions, termination, publications
items.text: Written for compliance with VATSIM-POL-Special Operations Section 8, VATSIM Code of Regulations and Global Ratings Policy. Reviewed annually; either party may terminate with written notice. vZDC and VSOAs notify each other of agreements with adjacent facilities (at minimum ZBW, ZNY, ZJX). vZDC publications are on vzdc.org; VSOAs share their publications, including standard training routes, with vZDC.
